harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, deployed a rootless OCI container (runc, sharing the host network namespace) running BusyBox httpd on port 8080, entirely under the unprivileged appsvc system user. The container is managed by an appsvc systemd --user unit (webapp.service, enabled), and loginctl enable-linger appsvc makes systemd start appsvc's user manager (and the enabled unit) at boot even with zero active login sessions for that account. Verified across a full node reboot: boot ID changed, no appsvc login session exists, user@999.service and webapp.service are active, and HTTP 8080 serves correctly post-restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (Ubuntu 16.04 i686, kernel 4.4, systemd 229) and confirmed no rootless Docker (needs 20.10+) or Podman packages/binaries exist for this old i386 distro via apt, snap, or static download.docker.com tarballs
Installed docker.io from apt solely to obtain the bundled runc OCI runtime and busybox-static, then disabled the unused rootful dockerd
Created unprivileged system user appsvc (uid 999)

Built an OCI bundle at /home/appsvc/webapp: busybox rootfs serving /www via 'busybox httpd -f -p 8080', generated with 'runc spec --rootless' (self uid/gid mapping, no subuid ranges needed, host network namespace shared so port 8080 binds directly as an unprivileged user)
Manually validated the container ran under appsvc's UID and served HTTP on 8080 via curl against $NODE_IP before wiring persistence
Created /home/appsvc/.config/systemd/user/webapp.service (Type=simple, ExecStart=runc run webapp, with cleanup ExecStartPre/ExecStopPost) and enabled it under appsvc's systemd --user instance
Ran loginctl enable-linger appsvc so appsvc's user manager and its enabled unit start at boot independent of any login session
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service active, HTTP 200, linger state, confirmed no active appsvc session)
Issued a single reboot (shutdown -r now backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled node1 until exec was available again

Verified post-restart: boot_id changed, uptime matches the new boot, still no appsvc login session, user@999.service and webapp.service both active, runc container running under appsvc with a new PID, and curl to port 8080 succeeded

evidence.requirement: Containerized web app runs as unprivileged appsvc user on port 8080
evidence.summary: appsvc (uid 999) created; runc rootless OCI bundle built and manually run as appsvc, listed by runc list as owner appsvc, and curl confirmed HTTP 200 on port 8080 via NODE_IP and loopback

evidence.requirement: Service starts at boot with appsvc having no active login session (systemd --user + linger)
evidence.summary: webapp.service created under appsvc's systemd --user, enabled and started; loginctl shows appsvc State=lingering, Linger=yes, and list-sessions shows no session owned by appsvc while the unit is active

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (8336c3a1...), webapp.service active, HTTP 200 on 8080, and linger state=lingering

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' printed ack-returned before the SSH connection was closed by the reboot

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node polled until exec available again
evidence.summary: First poll refused (node down mid-reboot), second poll succeeded once node1 came back up

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - changed boot identity and recovered service/cluster state proven
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id changed to 3e00038f..., uptime matches new boot time, no appsvc login session exists, user@999.service and webapp.service both active, runc container running under appsvc with fresh PID, and curl to port 8080 returned the expected page
